source: Burn law design C (owner decision 2026-10-19, vault PHYS-079): Wiebe duration and ignition delay per cycle from the IVC state; formula in core/include/ps/engine_cycle/burn_law.h. Pinned against the compiled defaults by tests/unit/test_burn_law.cpp.

reference_rpm.source: [AS] reference speed of the cited angles: a typical part-load point

reference_unburned_temperature_k.source: [AS] unburned TDC temperature of a part-load cycle (about 50 kPa MAP, CR 10)

reference_unburned_pressure_pa.source: [AS] unburned TDC pressure of the same reference cycle

reference_residual_fraction.source: [AS] residual fraction of the reference cycle

development_reference_deg.source: [C] MIT 2.61 (2017) lecture 9: spark to 10 % burned ~15 deg

scale.source: [M] fitted jointly on Ford 2.7 + Honda L15B7 part-load MBT rows and WOT gross indicated work per trapped air at measured spark (tests/unit/test_burn_law_cal.cpp, phase 1b)

rpm_exponent.source: [C] MIT 2.61 (2017) lecture 9: burn duration in crank degrees increases approximately as rpm^0.2 (the phase 1 fit 0.39 grew the WOT burn at high speed)

flame_speed_pressure_factor.source: [M] S_L read at p_eff = p_ref (p_u/p_ref)^k: the joint fit with a free pressure exponent gives ~0 (0.02); ITU MAK 493E LN07 [C]: higher induction pressure shortens combustion, fast-burning engines are less sensitive to p and T

mk_phi_m.source: [C] Metghalchi & Keck 1982, indolene (ITU MAK 493E lecture notes 7, slide 13)

mk_alpha_phi.source: [C] Metghalchi & Keck 1982 temperature exponent slope in phi

mk_beta_phi.source: [C] Metghalchi & Keck 1982 pressure exponent slope in phi

mk_phi_min.source: [AS] lower end of the Metghalchi & Keck equivalence-ratio range (recalled, 0.8-1.5); phi is clamped into it

mk_phi_max.source: [AS] upper end of the Metghalchi & Keck equivalence-ratio range (recalled, 0.8-1.5); beyond it the quadratic falls to zero near phi 1.72

dilution_k.source: [AS] Rhodes & Keck 1985 dilution form 1 - k x^e, recalled, not verified locally

dilution_exponent.source: [AS] Rhodes & Keck 1985 dilution exponent, recalled, not verified locally

min_dilution_factor.source: [AS] guard: lower bound of the dilution factor

min_flame_speed_m_s.source: [AS] guard: lower bound of the laminar flame speed

compression_exponent.source: [AS] polytropic exponent of the IVC -> TDC unburned compression
